benefits: $180,000 CAD valued over four years ($45,000 per year)
Membership in a community of President's International Scholars from different academic, geographic and cultural backgrounds

eligibility: Be a high-school student entering the first year of an undergraduate degree at York in Fall 2027
Hold international student status and be subject to international tuition fees during studies at York
Demonstrate strong academic performance, leadership skills and active involvement in volunteer work and extracurricular activities
Have a minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent
Be officially nominated by a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official (maximum of two nominations per school per year)
requirements: Apply to and receive an admission offer-eligible application for an undergraduate program at York for Fall 2027, and obtain a York University Reference Number
Submit the online scholarship application using the York Reference Number
Personal statement of maximum 500 words explaining why you are an exceptional candidate, speaking to professional goals, leadership, volunteer work and extracurricular activities
List of Extracurricular Activities & Community Involvement (maximum of 3)
Financial profile indicating the estimated total funding you will have to support your studies over the next three to four years
Official nomination form and signed reference letter on school letterhead from a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official
documents: Online scholarship application with York Reference Number
Official nomination form completed by the nominator
Reference letter signed and on the school's official letterhead, highlighting academic achievement and extracurricular/community involvement
Optional additional reference letter highlighting community involvement
selection_criteria: Academic excellence (highest academic calibre from around the world)

Recipients, known as President's International Scholars, represent students of the highest academic calibre from around the world.

applicant_utility.summary: Worth CAD $45,000 per year ($180,000 over four years), this is York's flagship entrance award for international high school students entering Fall 2027. You cannot apply directly: you must first apply to York admissions, then use your York reference number in the scholarship portal by January 27, 2027, and your school must nominate you by February 4, 2027. Plan backwards from those dates, because only two students per school can be nominated each year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-tier international high school students with roughly 80%+ average who can document sustained volunteering and extracurricular leadership and who can persuade their school to use one of its two nomination slots on them
application_readiness_checklist: Submit your York undergraduate application as early as possible; the scholarship portal needs the York reference number it generates, and late admission applications compress the whole timeline
Secure your school's nomination before January: only two students per school per year are accepted, so confirm early in the fall with your guidance counsellor
Draft the 500-word personal statement around concrete professional goals, leadership evidence and community impact, not generic ambition
Assemble a tight record of volunteer work and extracurriculars (max 3) and awards (max 3), with dates and roles
Prepare the financial profile: an honest estimate of total funding available for your 3-4 years, since York uses need context alongside merit
Brief your nominator in writing on the February 4, 2027 deadline and the letter requirements (signed, on school letterhead)
common_rejection_risks: Losing the school nomination race: two slots per school per year often go to the highest-profile students, so asking in April or later can mean you never get one
Nominator misses the February 4, 2027 deadline; York only emails the nomination link after you submit your own application, so any delay on your side cascades
Final admission average below the 80% minimum, including translation/conversion surprises for non-Ontario curricula
A personal statement that lists achievements without evidence of leadership and community commitment, which is what the selection criteria actually reward
Applying to York admission too late in the cycle, leaving no time to complete the scholarship portal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The official terms publish only the $45,000/year value and do not itemize covered expenses, so budget separately for residence and meal plans, University Health Insurance Plan, flights, visa costs and personal spending; the 4-year housing guarantee from York does not remove those housing bills
document_audit: The reference letter must be signed and printed on the school's official letterhead; a generic counsellor email is not the same document
Only 3 extracurriculars and 3 awards can be listed, so choose those with verifiable impact rather than padding the total
The financial profile asks for estimated total funding for the full degree, not family income documents, so prepare the figures in advance
alerts: PISE cannot be combined with York's automatic entrance scholarships: if you win PISE you receive the higher-value award instead, so do not count on stacking $37,500 of entrance scholarships on top
The portal opens November 1, 2026 and closes January 27, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. EST; the separate February 4 deadline covers only the nominator's submission
Students admitted to Computer Science, Cybersecurity or Engineering face extra restrictions on the automatic entrance scholarship, which makes PISE the more relevant award in those programs
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application first, scholarship portal second, nominator third: York releases the nomination link to your school official only after your own application is in, so your submission date gates everyone else's
